summary: Bing Chen worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He served as a professor at the Chengdu Academy of Social Sciences from around 1981 to 1987 and became a professor at Sichuan University around 1987.

Bingtao Ma specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned an MA from Peking University by 2008 and completed a PhD under the supervision of Xue Yu at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (attested 2015).

Biraja Sankar Guha worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. Educated at Scottish Church College, Calcutta University, and Harvard University (AM 1920, PhD 1924), he founded the Indian Anthropological Institute and directed the Anthropological Survey of India (1945–1954).

Birgit Kellner works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She earned a doctorate at Hiroshima University under Shoryu Katsura. Her career includes posts at Heidelberg University, the University of Vienna, and directorships at the Austrian Academy of Sciences and IKGA.
Biscoe Hale Wortham was an Indology scholar. He studied at Trinity College, Cambridge in 1863 and at Trinity College, Oxford from 1863 to 1868, where he received his BA.

Bisheshwar Nath Reu worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. After studying under Gaurishankar Hirachand Ojha (~1910–1916), he served from circa 1919 to 1950 as superintendent at Sumer Public Library and head of Government Museum Jodhpur and Maharaja Man Singh Pustak Prakash.

Biswajit Biswas works in religious studies and Indology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Rajat Kanti Das and held an appointment as a research scholar/fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Biswanath Banerjee worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies under Helmut Hoffmann (~1956–1959), served at Visva-Bharati University from 1967 to 1991, and was president of The Asiatic Society.
Blain Auer works in Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He earned his PhD from Harvard University (2002–2009) and was appointed professor at the University of Lausanne in 2013.
Blanche Christine Olschak worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Graz (~1933–1937) and studied under Constantin Régamey and Thupten Wangyal in 1946.
Bo Jiang works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Jiang earned a PhD at Columbia University under the supervision of Robert A. F. Thurman.

Bo Utas is a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at Uppsala University (~1958–1973) under Stig Wikander and Henrik Samuel Nyberg, later serving there as professor from circa 1987 to 2003.
Bo-Kwang Han is a scholar in Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Dongguk University (attested 2004, 2015) and taught Silwon Suk.
Bohumil Sládeček was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the Faculty of Arts of Charles University, earning his PhD under the supervision of Josef Zubatý.

Bojan Čop was a linguist specializing in Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Karel Oštir at the University of Ljubljana, earning a PhD, and served there as full professor of comparative Indo-European linguistics from 1972 to 1990.

Bokar Rinpoche worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Kalu Rinpoche (~1967–1989), held a post at Bokar Monastery (~1984–2004), and taught Shenpen Hookham, Lama Palden Drolma, Ogyen Trinley Dorje, and Khenpo Lodrö Dönyö.

Bong Seok Joo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. Joo completed undergraduate studies at UC Berkeley and earned a PhD from Princeton University under Stephen F. Teiser, also studying with Jacqueline I. Stone, Yang Lu, and Lewis Lancaster.

Bongkil Chung works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. After earning a PhD at Michigan State University under George C. Kerner, Chung served on the faculty at Florida International University, including from 1991 to 1992 and as professor of philosophy (attested 2012).

Borayin Larios works in Indology and religious studies. Educated at the University of Freiburg and Heidelberg University, Larios held posts at Heidelberg, the University of Vienna, the French Institute of Pondicherry, and the École française d'Extrême-Orient.

Boris Aleksandrovich Larin was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv under scholars including Friedrich Knauer and Sergey Oldenburg, later serving as professor at Saint Petersburg State University from 1922 and from 1962 to 1964.
